title: Daily physics — Wednesday, 11 November 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred ordering, not a most-read or most-downloaded list. The papers are only days old and citation evidence is sparse, so the ordering relies mainly on independently findable discussion, publication/release signals, cross-listing, and concrete results rather than readership metrics.

sections.title: New Constraints on the Ultrahigh Energy Neutrino Flux from the First Array-Wide Search with the Askaryan Radio Array
sections.abstract: The ARA Collaboration reports its first array-wide diffuse ultra-high-energy neutrino search, with no candidates and a flux upper limit from 50 to 1000 EeV.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report zero events on an expected background of 0.13 ± 0.01 (stat.) +0.05/−0.06 (syst.) and an upper limit they describe as the strongest from 50–1000 EeV; they also exclude some trans-GZK proton-source models at 90% confidence.
sections.evidence_type: observational; 10.6 years of data from all five South Pole ARA stations, with detector and neutrino simulations used in the search
sections.unique_caveat: This is a null search, not a neutrino detection; exposure depends on ice optical properties, the Askaryan-emission model, and the neutrino–nucleon cross section. The authors estimate the cross-section contribution to exposure uncertainty at about 150% at high energies.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: An independent neutrino-news roundup highlighted the result; it combines all five ARA stations and 10.6 years of livetime with a new array-wide flux constraint. The companion methodology paper is part of the same analysis, not an independent confirmation.

sections.title: Tidal potential measured with distant optical clocks
sections.abstract: Fibre-linked strontium and ytterbium clocks 692 km apart measure tidal changes in gravitational potential over 353 days, separate lunar- and solar-frequency semidiurnal components, and model precision using the actual sampling.
sections.claimed_result: The authors measure a response of 0.95 ± 0.11 to the combined solid-Earth and ocean-loading tide and 1.01 ± 0.13 for the lunar semidiurnal group, while separating lunar and solar-frequency contributions.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; strontium and ytterbium optical clocks connected by a phase-stabilized fibre link, with 545.9 hours of retained measurements across five campaigns
sections.unique_caveat: The diurnal and ocean-loading components have signal-to-noise ratios near unity; gaps, sampling aliases, and daily laboratory variations limit their precision.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed between optics and geophysics and reports an actual long-baseline clock measurement rather than a proposed sensitivity; the authors quantify multiple tidal components and provide a sampling-aware precision model.

sections.title: Search for heavy top quark partners with charge 5/3 in the single-lepton final state in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
sections.abstract: CMS searches 13 TeV proton-proton collision data for pair-produced charge-5/3 vector-like quarks in conventional top–W and exotic top–charged-Higgs decay modes, and sets mass-dependent cross-section limits.
sections.claimed_result: CMS reports no significant excess and excludes masses up to 1630 GeV for the top–W mode and up to 1740 GeV for the top–charged-Higgs mode when the charged Higgs mass is 800 GeV.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; CMS proton-proton collision data at 13 TeV collected during 2016–2018, corresponding to 138 fb⁻¹
sections.unique_caveat: The exclusions assume the specified decay chains and branching fractions; they do not cover arbitrary mixtures of vector-like-quark decay modes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The analysis has a CMS public-results record (B2G-24-005) and was submitted to Physical Review D; it uses 138 fb⁻¹ of LHC data and gives the first limits for the stated charged-Higgs decay scenario.

sections.title: Nonperturbative string dynamics in a (2+1)D lattice gauge theory on a superconducting quantum processor
sections.abstract: The authors use a 63-qubit superconducting processor to measure electric-string dynamics in a two-dimensional Z₂ lattice gauge theory with dynamical matter across confined and deconfined regimes.
sections.claimed_result: The authors observe rapid charge and flux spreading in the deconfined regime, enhanced matter occupation near a pair-creation resonance, and suppressed spreading at strong electric fields, with circuits reaching 15 second-order Trotter steps.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; 63 superconducting qubits, including 12 ancillas, with ancilla checks, noise rescaling, and classical reference calculations
sections.unique_caveat: Hardware noise and finite circuit depth limit the evolution time; tensor-network comparisons are restricted to times where bond-dimension convergence is obtained.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The experiment brings a concrete nonperturbative gauge-dynamics problem to a 63-qubit device and uses local Gauss-law constraints as an error-detection resource, supported by spatially resolved measurements.

sections.title: Tracing the Epoch of Reionization through extreme emission line galaxies around Cosmic Noon
sections.abstract: The authors assemble and spectroscopically validate a sample of 229 extreme-emission-line galaxies at redshifts about 1.0–1.7, assessing them as lower-redshift analogues of galaxies associated with reionization.
sections.claimed_result: The authors identify 102 Hβ+[O III] emitters near z=1.7 and 127 Hα emitters near z=1.0; they report compact, low-mass, strongly star-forming systems whose properties resemble z>5 JWST extreme emitters.
sections.evidence_type: observational; CANDELS/EGS photometry and data products, validated with ground- and space-based spectroscopy including JWST/NIRSpec
sections.unique_caveat: The proposed reionization connection is an analogy from cosmic-noon galaxies, not a direct measurement of the z>6 reionization population; photometric selection purities are below 100%.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv record says accepted for Astronomy & Astrophysics; spectroscopy from MMT/MMIRS, Keck/MOSFIRE, HST/WFC3, JWST/NIRSpec, and GTC/OSIRIS+ checks the sample.

sections.title: High-Speed Control of a Fluxonium Qubit via Picosecond Pulses from Josephson Digital Circuits
sections.abstract: The authors propose two single-flux-quantum pulse protocols for fast fluxonium control and report simulated single-qubit gate fidelities above 99.99%.
sections.claimed_result: Multilevel simulations indicate that flux-channel pulse packets provide robust high-fidelity control, while phase-shifted flux and charge sequences can shorten gates without losing the reported high fidelity.
sections.evidence_type: computational; multilevel simulations of fluxonium dynamics under picosecond single-flux-quantum pulses
sections.unique_caveat: The quoted fidelities are simulation results, not a hardware demonstration; performance depends on device parameters, flux bias, pulse design, and modeled control errors.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The work has a verified DOI and is listed as an accepted paper in Physical Review Applied; it links Josephson digital pulse generation with low-frequency fluxonium control.

sections.title: Probing for anisotropies at different angular scales in the arrival directions of the cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory
sections.abstract: The Pierre Auger Collaboration applies a von Mises–Fisher model to search for ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray arrival-direction excesses across angular scales using the Observatory’s Phase I data.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find the most significant excess to be a dipole in the 8–16 EeV bin, consistent with prior Auger findings, and report indications of a Centaurus-region intermediate-scale excess above 32 EeV.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Pierre Auger Observatory events above 4 EeV from 1 January 2004 through 31 December 2022
sections.unique_caveat: The higher-energy feature is not a source identification or discovery; the abstract calls it an indication, and more exposure is needed to establish its persistence.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It combines the Observatory’s full 2004–2022 Phase I exposure (123,000 km² sr yr) with a method that treats multiple angular scales consistently.

sections.title: Leveraging Lensing-driven Early Warnings: Joint Detectability of lensed Gravitational Waves and their LSST Optical Counterparts
sections.abstract: The authors simulate lensed binary-neutron-star and neutron-star–black-hole mergers for the O5 observing run and estimate how often LSST could detect their lensed kilonova counterparts.
sections.claimed_result: For the simulated O5 population, the authors estimate that roughly 60% of detectable lensed BNS kilonovae and 10% of NSBH kilonovae would be visible in a single LSST exposure.
sections.evidence_type: forecast/proposal; simulated lensed-merger populations and benchmark lensed-kilonova light curves evaluated against LSST bands and exposure limits
sections.unique_caveat: Detectability depends on assumed merger and lens populations, kilonova light-curve models, and survey exposure limits; no lensed counterpart is observed in this study.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It is cross-listed across high-energy astrophysics and cosmology and quantifies a gravitational-wave/optical follow-up pathway using LSST exposure limits; the result is a forecast rather than a detection.
